result: The authors determined a 2.9-Å resolution crystal structure of the AFF4(2-73)-P-TEFb-AMPPNP complex, revealing that AFF4 residues 34-66 bind to the CycT1 subunit of P-TEFb through extensive hydrophobic and hydrogen bonding interactions, while making no stable contacts with CDK9. The structure shows AFF4 adopts an extended conformation and induces conformational changes in CycT1 upon binding.

result: Interface mutations in both AFF4 and CycT1 reduce binding affinity in vitro and impair AFF4-dependent transcriptional stimulation in cells. Mutations of buried hydrophobic residues (Pro33/Leu34, Phe35, Met55/Leu56) in the structured binding region (residues 33-66) show the most severe effects, while mutations in flanking disordered regions (residues 3-32) show smaller but significant effects.

result: AFF4 and Tat make direct contacts when both are bound to P-TEFb, with Tat enhancing AFF4 binding affinity by approximately 11-fold. Structural superposition positions Tat adjacent to AFF4, creating an intersubunit binding pocket. Mutations in the predicted AFF4-Tat interface differentially affect P-TEFb binding in the presence versus absence of Tat, supporting direct AFF4-Tat interactions.
status_reasoning: The evidence for AFF4-Tat interactions is strong and multifaceted. Quantitative binding measurements show consistent ~11-fold enhancement of affinity by Tat for both AFF4(2-73) and AFF4(2-363) fragments (C39, C40), suggesting the key Tat-binding residues are within residues 2-73 (C41). This differential rescue pattern strongly supports direct AFF4-Tat contacts (C45, C53).

result: AFF4 binding reduces P-TEFb kinase activity by twofold but has minimal effect on Tat-P-TEFb activity. Tat-P-TEFb is 7-10 fold more active than P-TEFb alone. P-TEFb phosphorylates the GST-CTD substrate on both Ser2 and Ser5 residues.

result: P-TEFb phosphorylates RNA polymerase II and associated factors to trigger promoter escape and transcript elongation at paused genes. At many human genes, RNA polymerase II pauses after synthesizing 30-50 nucleotides, and P-TEFb-mediated promoter escape is rate-limiting. P-TEFb cycles between inactive and active complexes.

result: Super Elongation Complexes (SECs) containing P-TEFb, AFF1-4 scaffolds, and other elongation factors stimulate transcription elongation through multiple mechanisms. AFF proteins form intrinsically disordered scaffolds that bind partners through short dispersed binding sites. Despite their importance, SEC architecture was poorly understood at the time of this study.
